haiku-low.q1: No. Cursors are written to Redis key cursors:<docId> and published on presence:<docId>. They never go through the document service or Postgres.
haiku-low.q2: At most one per 50 ms per client. The node drops faster updates silently; the throttle timestamp is kept in node memory, not Redis.
haiku-low.q3: It holds that cursor as that connId's pending cursor, replacing any older held one, and draws nothing for that tab until appliedRev catches up.
haiku-low.q4: It calls transformPosition from its rev to appliedRev and draws the result. If transformPosition throws HistoryGone, the cursor is dropped until the next one arrives.
haiku-low.q5: Each tab has its own connId, but the client shows one caret per user, from the most recent accepted cursor. The avatar stays until the user's last tab leaves.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, within 2 s. After the user's gateway node dies, within 40 s, with a limit of 45 s.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis: conns, users, cursors, node-conns, node:<nodeId> and nodes, per tab and per user. Node heartbeat refreshes node:<nodeId> every 10 s with 30 s TTL. Presence records have no TTL.
haiku-low.q8: Live nodes' sweep, every 10 s, finds dead node ids whose node:<id> key is gone, runs the leave script per connection, and publishes leave. Subscribed nodes forward it to their sockets.
haiku-low.q9: The sender's node publishes the cursor on presence:<docId>. Each subscribed node with local sockets on that document forwards it to its sockets, except the sender.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes and writes before reading the snapshot, so a user joining in between is in the snapshot or sends a live join. Duplicate joins are ignored. Leave and cursor handling is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q11: The snapshot includes each tab's last cursor and seq, including idle tabs, so the newly joined client draws the idle caret.
haiku-low.q12: Each cursor carries seq. The receiver drops any cursor whose seq is not higher than the last seq seen from that connId.

sonnet.q1: No. Cursors never go through the document service and never go to Postgres; they are stored in Redis (cursors:<docId>) and published on presence:<docId>.
sonnet.q2: At most one cursor per 50 ms per client. The node drops faster updates silently (compared with last accepted arrival time, kept in node memory, not Redis).
sonnet.q3: It holds it as that connId's pending cursor (replacing any older held one) and draws nothing for that tab yet. When appliedRev advances, it re-runs the transform step on held cursors.
sonnet.q4: The client calls transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev) and draws the caret at the result. If it throws HistoryGone (revision too old), the cursor is dropped until the next one arrives.
sonnet.q5: Avatars are per user (one avatar), and the client shows one caret per user, from the tab that sent the most recent accepted cursor. The user disappears (leave with userGone: true) only when the last tab closes (or is swept); closing one of several tabs only removes that tab's caret.
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: within 2 s (one publish and one forward). Node death: within 40 s worst case (30 s key expiry plus up to 10 s to next sweep); limit for the change is 45 s.
sonnet.q7: In Redis, per document and per connection/tab (conns, users, cursors hashes/sets keyed by docId, plus per-node node-conns). Only node:<nodeId> has a TTL (30 s), refreshed by the node's heartbeat every 10 s; presence records themselves have no TTL and are removed on close or by a sweep.
sonnet.q8: Surviving nodes' sweep (every 10 s) removes them: for each node whose node:<id> key expired, it reads node-conns and runs the leave script per connection, publishes leave (only the node whose script removed the tab, and only if last tab), then removes the dead id from nodes. Nodes holding other users' sockets are subscribed and forward the leave to their clients.
sonnet.q9: The node writes the cursor to cursors:<docId> in Redis, then publishes it on presence:<docId>. Every node with a local socket on that document (including the sender's own node, via the same channel) receives it and forwards it to its sockets, except the sender.
sonnet.q10: By ordering: the node subscribes to presence:<docId> and writes its own records first, then reads the snapshot. A user who joins in between is either in the snapshot or sends a live join; a join seen twice is ignored by the client.
sonnet.q11: The snapshot, read from Redis cursors and conns, includes every connected user and each tab's last cursor and seq, including idle tabs.
sonnet.q12: Each client increments seq per cursor message; the receiver drops any cursor whose seq is not higher than the last seq seen from that connId.
